summary_plain: Moves about 25 arcseconds per hour across 18 images over 24.6 hours. It matches the known asteroid 3095 Omarkhayyam (1980 RT2).

orbit.reported_orbit: The arc is too short to fix one orbit, so this is the most circular of the 747 sampled orbits that fit the detections; the clones show the range.

known_object.observer: SPHEREx (geocentric JPL predictions corrected with the spacecraft position from the FITS headers)

scores.definition: Rule-based ranking score in [0, 1]: motion_consistency x snr x (1 - artifact_likelihood). It orders candidates for review. It is not a probability.

explanation.text: Detected in 18 SPHEREx exposures spanning 24.6 hours. It moves 25.0 arcseconds per hour toward position angle 63 degrees. A straight-line motion plus orbital-parallax fit leaves 1.09 arcseconds of scatter. SPHEREx's own orbital parallax puts it roughly 2.10 AU away (range 1.34 to 4.77 AU). Its faintest detection has a signal-to-noise ratio of 4.5. Its positions match JPL's prediction for 3095 Omarkhayyam (1980 RT2) to within 1.9 arcseconds at every epoch.
